slides.heading: Year 1 — Autumn 2, Week 2
slides.sub: New content taught directly, practised in words/sentences and applied in reading and dictation.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "a-e" (/eɪ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="cake" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="cake"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Echo Star sits at the far end of the word and can't shout her own name — instead she beams her light back over the consonant in between to wake up the 'a' and make it say its own name, 'ay'.

character.name: Echo Star
character.blurb: Echo Star sits quietly at the end of the word, and instead of making her own sound, she beams her light backwards to wake the letter across the gap.

slides.pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'ai' in rain and 'ay' in day — here the letters split apart around a consonant, so it's called a split digraph.
slides.formation_cue: This sound splits in two: write 'a', then a consonant in the middle, then 'e' right at the end — like cake, where 'a' and 'e' are two ends of a bridge with 'k' standing on it.
slides.action: Children point to an imaginary letter far ahead, then mime a beam travelling backward from their fingertip to their other hand, saying 'ay' as it arrives.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="cake" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="cake"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.tip: The 'ere' ending says /eer/ — it's the exact same letters as the ending of 'there' and 'where', but those two sound the same as each other while 'here' sounds different.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "are" (/eə/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="scared" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="feeling_scared"><image href="data:image/png;base64, " x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Take care and share: a-r-e can say /air/, just like the air in chair.
slides.pronunciation_note: Another way to write the /air/ sound children already know from 'chair'. Say it the same way as 'air': care, share, scared.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'a', then 'r', then 'e', close together — three letters, one sound.
slides.action: Children hold out both hands as if sharing something with a friend, saying 'air'.
